A multi-step heating strategy which involves up-heating to and dwelling at several temperatures between 900 and 1170 C has been adopted for the homogenization treatment. A total dwell time at high temperatures reached 50 h.

The hot extrusion was conducted at 1120 C with a 260 MN extrusion force and an extrusion ratio of 4:1. A two-pass hot extrusion was conducted in order to promote plastic deformation and reﬁne grain structure.
Some of the samples were then subjected to a standard heat treatment, e.g., solution treatment at 1135 C for 4 h followed by air cooling
then annealing at 830 C for 6 h followed by air cooling
and ﬁnally ageing at 760 C for 6 h followed by air cooling.

attributes.morphology: large polygonal or irregular-shaped primary γ' particles; irregular-shaped secondary γ' and spherical tertiary γ'

evidence.quote: The grain interior is dominated by large polygonal or irregular-shaped primary g0 particles. A small number of irregular-shaped secondary g0 particles and a high population of spherical tertiary g0 particles are located in the g channels between primary g0 precipitates.
The majority of g grains are demonstrated to be fully recrystallized while the rest are sub-structured.
the majority of GB primary g0 particles are identiﬁed to be deformed g0.

attributes.morphology: large and irregular-shaped in central region; finer and increasingly regularly-shaped in half-radius region; finest and nearly cuboidal in peripheral region

evidence.quote: the central region has the largest and most irregular-shaped secondary g0 while the half-radius region contains remarkably ﬁner and increasingly regularly-shaped secondary g0. The peripheral region has the ﬁnest secondary g0 which show a nearly cuboidal morphology.
There is a small volume fraction of ultraﬁne tertiary g0 present in between the secondary g0 precipitates.

attributes.size: finer than in hot-extruded state; core regions have relatively larger secondary γ' than peripheral regions

evidence.quote: the heat-treated samples show slightly coarsened grain structure but much fewer GB primary g0 and much ﬁner secondary g0 particles. The secondary g0 precipitates generally show a near-cuboidal morphology.

attributes.size: peripheral region relatively fine, interior much larger

evidence.quote: the peripheral region of the ingot contains relatively ﬁne equiaxed grains while the interior is dominated by much larger grains.
It is obvious that the ingot still contains an extremely coarse cast grain structure (Fig. 3a).

attributes.size: average grain size in peripheral region ~5 μm (ASTM 12); core region ~10 μm (ASTM 10)

evidence.quote: The average grain size in the peripheral region is determined to be around 5 mm in diameter (or ASTM 12 level) and that of the core region is around 10 mm (or ASTM 10 level).
It is clear that the samples from different regions all show a high density of twin boundaries, indicating that twinning could have been the main deformation and recrystallization mechanism.
According to the pole ﬁgures, samples from different regions show more or less <100> texture.
Samples from the core regions even show pronounced <111> texture.
There are also a number of stacking faults (SFs) present in the precipitates as evidenced by both the TEM micrograph and diffraction pattern shown in Fig. 12b
GB bulging together with some g grains which are free of dislocations was also observed in the hot-extruded sample

attributes.location: intersection of stacking faults on different crystal planes

evidence.quote: HRTEM image (Fig. 16d) further demonstrates that some stacking faults in different crystal planes have even intersected with each other to form Lomer-Cottrell (LC) locks.
stacking faults still extended through both g and g0 precipitates during deformation; see Fig. 17aec.

direct forging on the heavily-alloyed GH4151 ingot was also found to cause severe cracking; see Fig. 4a. In addition to a number of large cracks present in the forged billet, there are also considerable micro-cracks in the interior (Fig. 4c).

Extensive twinning happened and played a crucial role in accommodating large and sudden macroscopic plastic deformation during hot extrusion.
Dynamic recrystallization happened through twinning and grain boundary bulging, leading to signiﬁcant grain reﬁnement.
This suggests that the deformation of the primary g0 precipitates mainly occurred by dislocation slipping during hot extrusion
Given that GB bulging and twinned structure are usually the characteristics of DRX, their presence indicates that DRX has happened during hot extrusion.
